Renormalization-Group Flow of the Proportion Mediated

Source: R/rg-flow.R
RgFlowResult.Rd

S7 class for the scale-indexed proportion mediated g_l = NIE_l / TE_l estimated on data coarse-grained to aggregation scale l (block size m). Under the coarse-graining operator T_m – which replaces each within-cluster block of m units by its mean – g_l flows with m, and the flow is governed by the mediation beta-function.

This is the classical proportion mediated (a ratio of effects), not the package's P_med (a probability in [0, 1]); the two are different quantities and are deliberately named apart. See vignette("probmed") for P_med.

Usage

RgFlowResult(
  g = integer(0),
  g_ci = integer(0),
  g_se = integer(0),
  a_path = integer(0),
  b_path = integer(0),
  TE = integer(0),
  grad_norm = integer(0),
  phi_cluster = integer(0),
  m = integer(0),
  n_units = integer(0),
  n_clusters = integer(0),
  ci_level = integer(0),
  call = NULL
)

Arguments

g

Numeric: estimated proportion mediated at this scale.

g_ci

Numeric length-2: cluster-robust EIF Wald confidence interval.

g_se

Numeric: cluster-robust standard error.

a_path, b_path, TE

Numeric: the a, b, and total-effect components.

grad_norm

Numeric: Euclidean norm of the gradient of g in the five moments; bounds the bias induced by a moment perturbation of a given size.

phi_cluster

Numeric: per-cluster influence contributions, in cluster order. Retained so two scales estimated on the same clusters can be contrasted by rg_flow_contrast().

m

Numeric: aggregation scale (block size); 1 is the unit scale.

n_units

Integer: coarse-grained units retained at this scale.

n_clusters

Integer: clusters contributing at this scale.

ci_level

Numeric: confidence level.

call

Call: original call.

Details

g_l is a smooth functional of five second moments of (A, M, Y), so the efficient influence function is available in closed form and the plug-in estimator is already efficient in the linear-Gaussian case (no cross-fitting required). The sampling unit is the cluster, not the unit: influence contributions are aggregated to the cluster before their variance is taken.
